name: Sofrah Venue
author: ahmedmahgoup94

sections.description:
Sofrah Venue keeps a restaurant’s or cafe’s content in one place, so changing theme loses nothing:

  • Menus with sections, dishes, prices as you write them, dietary labels in your own words and an allergen notice per dish.
  • A venue allergen statement, required before any dish is published.
  • Opening hours in the venue’s time zone, and dated notices (closed, special hours, paused).
  • “Today”: mark a dish sold out, or available again, with one tap on a phone.
  • Two staff roles: Venue manager and Menu editor.
  • Six blocks: Menu, Hours and location, Notices, Table request, Request status and Contact details.
  • A setup checklist and a one-click import of two fictional demos (a restaurant and a cafe).

Deposits and events through WooCommerce

  • Optional table deposit, per guest or per booking, for parties above a size you choose. It is asked for only after a person at the venue confirms the request: Sofrah Venue creates a WooCommerce order and WooCommerce emails the guest a link to pay it with any payment method you have set up. Nothing is paid before you accept, so a declined request needs no refund.
  • If the booking is cancelled before the deposit is paid, the order is cancelled. If the venue cancels after payment, the deposit is refunded through the payment method where it allows refunds; otherwise the order tells staff to refund it. If the guest cancels after paying, the order notes it for your policy.
  • The guest’s status page shows whether the deposit is due, paid or refunded, with the payment link while it is due.
  • Set menus and events: mark any WooCommerce product with a date and time. The date shows on the product page, in the cart, at checkout and on the order; seats are WooCommerce stock; once the date has passed, the product can no longer be bought.
  • Compatible with WooCommerce’s order tables (HPOS) and the cart and checkout blocks.

Table requests are requests

Requests go through the free Five Star Restaurant Reservations plugin, which holds them and sends the emails. Sofrah Venue never shows a request as a confirmed table until a person at the venue confirms it in that plugin:

  • After sending, the guest reads “Request received – your table is not confirmed yet”, with your reply window and phone number.
  • The plugin’s automatic confirmation rules are kept off.
  • If sending stalls, the guest is told the request may not have arrived and is asked not to send it again straight away.
  • Each email to the guest links to a status page that shows where the request stands.
  • If a confirmed booking is later closed, Sofrah Venue emails the guest a short cancellation notice (the reservation plugin sends nothing in that case).
  • Free-text notes are off by default, so guests are not invited to type health details.

Requests stay off until every step of the setup checklist is done, including a test request you send and see arrive.

Privacy

Sofrah Venue stores no information about guests and makes no outside requests: no telemetry, no external fonts or scripts. Deposits and event tickets are WooCommerce orders, covered by WooCommerce’s own export and erase tools. Sofrah Venue adds WordPress personal-data export and erase tools for the requests the reservation plugin holds, and suggested privacy-policy text.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce, then Sofrah Venue.
  2. Optional, for table requests: install and activate Five Star Restaurant Reservations.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Venue setup, import a demo or fill in WooCommerce > Venue settings, and follow the checklist. Dishes, menus and notices are under Food menu.
  4. Optional: turn on deposits in WooCommerce > Venue settings after setting up a payment method in WooCommerce > Settings > Payments.
sections.faq:
Does it take online orders or payments?

Not food orders. Payments are for table deposits and for set menus or event tickets, through WooCommerce checkout. For food ordering, use a dedicated ordering plugin.

Which PHP version do table requests need?

Sofrah Venue itself runs on PHP 7.4 or later. Five Star Restaurant Reservations asks for PHP 8.0 or later; without it, guests see your phone and email instead of a form.
sections.changelog:
0.2.4

  • The demo import also finds the sample pictures in the Sofrah Venue theme (the Platera theme’s new name).

0.2.3

  • The confirmation shown after saving on the Today, Venue settings and Venue setup screens is kept for the current user on the server instead of being passed in the address, and the Today screen names a dish only to someone who may edit it.

0.2.2

  • New name: Sofrah Venue (slug and text domain sofrah-venue), formerly Platera Venue, because the name Platera is also used by other restaurant software. Settings, menus, notices and requests are kept.
  • The event date and time on WooCommerce products are saved only with a valid form nonce and the right to edit the product.
  • The two one-time admin notices (a dish kept as a draft, a closure saved) appear only on the dish and notice screens.
  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.3.

0.2.1

  • Contributors set to the author’s WordPress.org username. No change in behaviour.

0.2.0

  • Requires WooCommerce. Optional table deposits after a request is confirmed, paid through WooCommerce; dated set menus and events as WooCommerce products.
  • Admin: dishes, menus and notices under “Food menu”; Venue settings and Venue setup under WooCommerce. No branded top-level menu.
  • Translations loaded from the plugin’s languages folder; translation template included.
  • Declares compatibility with WooCommerce order tables (HPOS) and the cart and checkout blocks.

0.1.1

  • Author set to Ahmed Mahgoub; no change in behaviour.

0.1.0

  • First release for testing: menus, hours, notices, roles, six blocks, request wording and status page, setup checklist, two demos, privacy tools.
